cards.title: Identifiability of Population PK/PD Models
cards.claim: Structural identifiability concerns whether model parameters can be distinguished under ideal input-output data. In the source fixed-effects examples, the Fisher Information Matrix determinant (|MF|) had a continuous log-log relationship with residual variance and approached infinity as residual variance approached zero; the mixed-effects examples had a noninfinite asymptote. These are model- and design-dependent diagnostic conditions, not sufficient proof of global structural uniqueness. Random-effects parameters do not automatically follow the identifiability behavior of corresponding fixed-effects parameters and must be assessed separately.
limitations: Positive |MF| values alone are insufficient to confirm identifiability
Nonidentifiable models may also yield positive |MF| values for some residual variances

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
